answer: I would like to talk about a colleague whose sense of style everyone in our office notices. A person whose style I genuinely admire is a colleague of mine who always manages to look effortlessly elegant. She joined our consultancy about a year ago as a senior counsellor, and we often work together on university applications, so I see her almost every day. She never seems to be trying too hard, yet every outfit looks carefully considered. What I find impressive is how [[versatile]] her wardrobe is; she can look professional at work and stylish at a social event with equal ease. At the office she usually wears a simple salwar kameez or a sari in muted colours, and at weddings she looks even more graceful, without ever seeming overdressed. She favours simple, classic pieces over loud trends, which gives her a timeless, [[sophisticated]] look. I think what makes her stand out is her attention to small details, like how well things fit and the way colours [[complement]] one another. She once told me that dressing well is less about money and more about knowing what suits you, which struck me as genuinely wise. As for how I feel about her style, I find it quietly inspiring. Honestly, being around her has made me a little more thoughtful about my own appearance, and I now iron my shirts rather more carefully. I think the way you present yourself quietly shapes how others perceive you, and she understands that [[instinctively]].

followUps.q: Do you care much about fashion?
followUps.answer: Not a great deal. I like to look neat and presentable, especially for work, but I rarely follow trends. I prefer [[understated]] clothes that are comfortable and will not go out of style quickly.

followUps.q: What do people in your country usually wear on special occasions?
followUps.answer: Traditional clothes, mostly. Men wear a panjabi, especially at Eid, and women often wear colourful saris. Weddings are the most formal occasions, and people dress very elaborately for them.

note: Set her at my consultancy and added how I know her, what she actually wears (salwar kameez, sari) and how her style has affected me.
